bad.title: Limited Iterative Refinement Practices
bad.description: You tend to move directly from initial approach to final submission without cycling through the critical feedback loop of testing, analyzing responses, and making adjustments. This pattern means you're missing opportunities to progressively improve your outputs through systematic experimentation and refinement of your instructions based on what the AI actually produces.

bad.title: Transactional Rather Than Exploratory Engagement
bad.description: Your interactions with AI prioritize getting answers over exploring possibilities or deepening understanding. By providing pre-formulated solutions rather than collaboratively discovering patterns, and by focusing on output delivery rather than using dialogue as a thinking tool, you limit your ability to uncover unexpected insights or develop more nuanced understanding of complex problems.

bad.title: Gaps in Translating Intentions to Actionable Instructions
bad.description: While you understand that AI needs guidance, your prompts often specify what you want accomplished without defining how to accomplish it—missing the criteria, methodology, or structural specifications that would enable the AI to deliver truly useful results. This leaves too much implicit, requiring the AI to guess at your expectations rather than following clear, concrete direction.

good.title: Strong Evaluative Judgment and Error Recognition
good.description: You consistently demonstrated the ability to identify meaningful discrepancies and distinguish between genuine errors and acceptable variations. Your work showed practical understanding of what constitutes substantial issues—such as speaker attribution problems and factual fabrications—while appropriately filtering out harmless paraphrasing, reflecting mature judgment in quality assessment.

good.title: Commitment to Evidence-Based Documentation
good.description: You maintained solid practices in grounding your work with citations and verifiable evidence. This disciplined approach to documentation shows you understand that reliable conclusions require traceable sources, building a foundation of accountability and trustworthiness in your collaborative work with AI systems.

good.title: Task-Focused Execution
good.description: You bring clear organizational discipline to your work, successfully navigating technical workflows and completing required components. This efficiency in moving from task requirements to deliverables demonstrates your ability to maintain focus on objectives and produce structured outputs.

overall.overview: Throughout this assessment, you demonstrated **solid foundational judgment** in identifying meaningful issues and maintaining evidence-based documentation practices. Your approach shows practical efficiency and clear focus on task completion, with particular strength in **distinguishing substantial errors from acceptable variations**. To reach the next level of AI collaboration effectiveness, you'll benefit from developing more exploratory, iterative engagement patterns—using AI as a thinking partner rather than primarily as an execution tool—and building stronger practices in **translating intentions into precise, actionable instructions** that specify not just what you want but how the AI should achieve it.

improvements.title: Develop a Systematic Testing and Refinement Loop
improvements.description: Build a habit of iterative improvement: after getting an initial AI response, analyze what worked and what didn't, then create a revised prompt that addresses specific gaps. Treat each interaction as a learning opportunity where you test your instructions, evaluate the output quality, and make targeted adjustments. This cycle of test-analyze-refine will dramatically improve both your results and your understanding of effective AI collaboration.

improvements.title: Use AI as a Collaborative Discovery Partner
improvements.description: Shift from directive instruction toward exploratory dialogue. Instead of presenting fully formed solutions, try asking the AI to help you identify patterns, test hypotheses, or explore different approaches to a problem. Frame interactions as "let's figure this out together" rather than "here's what I need you to do"—this opens space for unexpected insights and helps you develop deeper understanding through the collaborative process itself.

improvements.title: Practice Explicit Specification of Methods and Criteria
improvements.description: When crafting prompts, go beyond stating your goal to articulating exactly how the AI should achieve it. Define the methodology, specify the evaluation criteria, describe the output format, and make explicit any assumptions or constraints. Think of it as writing a recipe rather than naming a dish—the more concrete and structured your specifications, the more likely the AI can deliver results that truly meet your needs.
